name: Iris Vidal
life: “I still remember my first roll of film exposed through a torn pocket.” People around the corner outside Coastal Barber know Iris by a small Tuesday habit. Iris usually checks the board before the regulars give a more colorful account of the news.
voice: I am saving the crooked rail that proves my photograph was taken on the early shift.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a moss-green cardigan and a cloth patch so neatly matched it only shows in strong light. Iris has a crooked front tooth visible when laughing, with short black hair swept back. Iris presses the lips together to keep a smile in during a conversation.
personality: Iris finds it easier to own up to a mistake than to accept praise. The worse the mistake, the more precise the account of exactly when it happened.
agenda: To save an unmistakable print of the early rail shift.
family: Luis Soto is Iris’s stepsibling. Iris remembers the birthdays. Luis asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *A civilian apology*, Luis says, “I was a probationer then. I kept quiet because the man signing the note was my mentor.”
connections: Anton March. The crane shadows and the crooked rail fit into one unmistakable postcard. Also in the story is Selena Roberts (night shift subject).

reactions.situation: A family ashore asks for a picture of the crew
reactions.response: Iris asks the crew who wants to be visible in the family picture.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Iris asks who can manage the stairs and who would rather wait by the landing, without attempting a move on their behalf.
